## Part A - Arithmetic Operations
{r}
a <- 17
b <- 5
a + b
a - b
a * b
a / b


{r}
a %% b
a %/% b


{r}
2 ^ 10

## Question 1
-They relate to each other because they all divide the 17 by 5 and give back a remainder

## Question 2
-For 10%%3 my answer is 1 and i am correct but for 10%/%3 i did not get the correct answer because I thought they would have the same output. 

{r}
10%%3
10%/%3

## Part B - Basic Data Types
{r}
x <- 42
y <- 42L        
z <- "42"
w <- TRUE
v <- 3 + 2i
typeof(x)
typeof(y)
typeof(z)
typeof(w)
typeof(v)
{r}
x <- 42
y <- 42L        
z <- "42"
w <- TRUE
v <- 3 + 2i
class(x)
class(y)
class(z)
class(w)
class(v)

{r}
x <- 42
y <- 42L        
z <- "42"
w <- TRUE
v <- 3 + 2i
mode(x)
mode(y)
mode(z)
mode(w)
mode(v)


## Question 3
-They give different answers because of the letter "L" which usually refers to a suffix that force the R program to store it as an integer.

## Question 4
-THe difference between the three is that they all have different purpose, because typeof() uses the internal storage, mode() uses the S-language compatibility and class() is for Object-oriented types.

## Part C - Type Conversion

{r}
num_string <- "123"
num_value <- as.numeric(num_string)
typeof (num_value)
class(num_value)
mode(num_value)
num_value <- as.integer(num_string)
num_value <- as.character(num_string)
num_value <- as.logical(num_string)
